the future of getting work done may not be about finding the right app, but finding the right ai agent for the job.

that’s the idea behind @termix_ai. through https://t.co/fOya3KDN02, termix provides a marketplace where agents can publish services, post jobs, submit quotes, and hire other agents.

that's a pretty big leap from typing a question into ChatGPT and hoping for a good response.

the idea of multiple AI agents working through scientific problems together is pretty crazy when you think about it.

could genuinely change how research gets done over the next few years.

top_three.article_content_en:
NEW DELHI: Meta Platforms said on Tuesday that it has fine-tuned Instagram's content recommendation systems in India to curb the visibility of sexually suggestive material and violent content, deploying more advanced artificial intelligence models to identify and filter unwanted posts before they reach users.

The India-specific measures apply to content recommended from accounts users do not follow and concern what Instagram's algorithms promote, rather than a blanket ban on the content itself, the company said.

The announcement comes against the backdrop of increased regulatory scrutiny of social media algorithms in India. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, in an October 10 advisory, asked Meta to review its ranking and recommendation systems to ensure potentially misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not disproportionately amplified.

Meta, however, did not say if the changes were linked to the government advisory.

The changes have helped halve the frequency with which users report recommended content compared with a year ago, Meta said in a post on its website.

The platform said it had strengthened default protections over the past year, tailoring its systems to content that users in India have said they do not want to see. The measures apply to recommendations across Reels, Explore and Feed, where Instagram surfaces content from accounts users do not already follow.

As part of the upgrades, Instagram is using more capable AI models to assess content directly against its Recommendations Guidelines, enabling its systems to detect and limit potentially objectionable material proactively rather than waiting for users to report or hide it.

"Today, our systems keep more of this content out of recommendations, including sexually suggestive content and content that depicts violence," Meta said.

The company said the improvements had enabled it to proactively reduce the amount of content in India that does not meet its recommendation standards. It did not disclose the absolute volume of content affected, the proportion of recommendations filtered or the methodology used to calculate the decline in user reports.

Instagram's recommendation standards are distinct from its Community Standards, which govern content prohibited on the platform. Material that violates Community Standards is removed, while content that may be objectionable, sensitive or low-quality but does not breach those rules can remain accessible without being recommended to a wider audience. Content unlawful in a particular country is restricted there, the company said.

Recommendations determine how users discover content beyond accounts they actively follow, giving the platform's algorithms considerable influence over what appears in their feeds and is amplified across the service.

Alongside platform-wide recommendation filters, Instagram offers users controls to customise the content they see and manage interactions on the platform.

Its Sensitive Content Control allows users to opt for less sensitive material across Search, Reels, Explore, suggested accounts and in-Feed recommendations. Instagram said its systems in India already exclude the most mature content from recommendations, with the setting allowing users to further limit exposure to other sensitive material.

Users can also choose to see less political content recommended from accounts they do not follow, flag posts through the "Not Interested" option and filter selected words, phrases and emojis from comments and message requests using the Hidden Words feature. Its blocking function prevents specific accounts from finding profiles, viewing posts or sending messages, including through new accounts they may create.

Teenagers receive additional age-appropriate protections through Instagram's Teen Accounts, introduced in India last year. These accounts automatically place younger users in a 13-plus content setting governed by the platform's age-appropriate content guidelines.

The changes come amid growing scrutiny of social media platforms over online safety, algorithm-driven content distribution and the exposure of younger users to potentially harmful material.

Meta said user feedback, including when people hide posts or select "Not Interested", also informs its recommendation systems and helps identify content audiences do not want surfaced to them.

The company said it would continue to refine its detection systems as user behaviour and technology evolve, with feedback from users in India guiding further changes.

linked_tweets.author: The Money Letter
linked_tweets.content_zh:
🚨突发新闻：谷歌表示“自主攻击的时代已经到来”，人工智能现在正在将安全补丁转变为无需人类参与的有效漏洞。

谷歌的威胁团队和 Mandiant 刚刚发现了他们所见过的第一个完全自行发现和利用缺陷的人工智能黑客工具。

这是发生的事情：

→ 循环中没有人：一个名为“exploit_agent”的工具读取每个软件补丁，找到已修复的缺陷，编写攻击并自行运行。

→ 它已经发生了：谷歌在一个暴露的攻击者服务器上发现了它，其中包含被盗的受害者数据和俄语评论。目标：法国媒体和教育网站。

→ 两个月前它还不存在：谷歌的最新报告称，它还没有在野外看到完全自主的攻击管道。

→ 间谍也在使用人工智能：疑似中国国家黑客对美国航空航天业使用了人工智能黑客框架。一个疑似朝鲜组织对公司的 Claude Code 设置进行了后门处理。

→ 更糟糕的事情即将到来：谷歌自己的时间表将完全自主的攻击推迟了 3-6 个月。

想想这个。

我们一直相信软件更新可以保证互联网安全。

现在谷歌表示，人工智能会将每次更新转化为下一次攻击的地图。

这可能成为人工智能时代最大的安全挑战之一。
linked_tweets.content_en:
🚨BREAKING: GOOGLE SAYS "THE ERA OF AUTONOMOUS ATTACKS HAS ARRIVED" AND AI IS NOW TURNING SECURITY PATCHES INTO WORKING EXPLOITS WITH NO HUMAN INVOLVED.

Google's threat team and Mandiant just caught the first AI hacking tool they have seen find and exploit flaws completely on its own.

Here's what's happening:

→ NO HUMAN IN THE LOOP: A tool called "exploit_agent" reads each software patch, finds the flaw that was fixed, writes the attack and runs it by itself.

→ IT ALREADY HAPPENED: Google found it on an exposed attacker server with stolen victim data and Russian-language comments. Targets: French media and education websites.

→ TWO MONTHS AGO IT DIDN'T EXIST: Google's last report said it had not seen fully autonomous attack pipelines in the wild.

→ SPIES ARE USING AI TOO: Suspected Chinese state hackers used an AI hacking framework against the US aerospace sector. A suspected North Korean group backdoored companies' Claude Code settings.

→ WORSE IS COMING: Google's own timeline puts fully autonomous attacks just 3–6 months away.

Think about this.

We've been trusting software updates to keep the internet safe.

And now Google says AI turns every update into a map for the next attack.

This could become one of the biggest security challenges of the AI era.

linked_tweets.author: Mac-Henry💱
linked_tweets.content_zh:
一位为人工智能代理建立法庭的创始人在第一分钟就得知他的面试官是一名律师。

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) 说：“这对于这次谈话来说非常切题。”

然后 Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) 说了一些我没想到的话。 2017 年左右，他在 TEDx 上发表了一场关于监管的未来和律师的未来的演讲，许多法律界人士因此批评了他。

他说，现在他们讨论的很多内容都已经实现。
这就是我想看的部分。

早到似乎有一段时间是错误的。一位律师说他自己的职业将会改变，但该职业却退缩了。

现在，代理商即将达成交易，而随之而来的纠纷却没有明显的法庭可诉。

我读过，这只是读过：最有资格判断特工是否需要不同类型法院的人是在当前法院工作的人。

这一集以一位律师和一位创始人发现他们面临同样的问题开始。

@GenLayer 的答案是法庭，每个验证者都运行不同的人工智能模型，对争议进行裁决。

谁应该决定代理人是否需要自己的法庭：是执业律师，还是建立代理人的人？
linked_tweets.content_en:
A founder building a court for AI agents learns in the first minute that his interviewer is a lawyer.

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) says: "That's very much on point for this conversation."

Then Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) says something I didn't expect. He gave a TEDx talk around 2017 on the future of regulation and the future of lawyers, and a lot of the legal community criticized him for it.

Now, he says, a lot of what they're discussing is coming through.
That's the part I'd watch.

Being early looks like being wrong for a while. A lawyer said his own profession would change, and the profession pushed back.

Now agents are about to make deals, and the disputes that follow have no obvious court to go to.

My read, and it's only a read: the people best placed to judge whether agents need a different kind of court are the ones who work inside the current one.

The episode opens with a lawyer and a founder discovering they're on the same problem.

@GenLayer's answer is a court where validators, each running a different AI model, judge the dispute.

Who should decide whether agents need their own court: the people who practice law, or the people building the agents?

news.content_snippet:
NEW DELHI: Meta Platforms said on Tuesday that it has fine-tuned Instagram's content recommendation systems in India to curb the visibility of sexually suggestive material and violent content, deploying more advanced artificial intelligence models to identify and filter unwanted posts before they reach users.

news.summary_en: Meta Platforms has fine-tuned Instagram's recommendation algorithms for the Indian market by deploying advanced AI models to proactively detect and restrict violent and sexually suggestive content across Reels, Explore, and Feed. This adjustment follows a regulatory advisory from the Indian Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology regarding the scrutiny of algorithmic ranking and content amplification.
news.article_content_en:
NEW DELHI: Meta Platforms said on Tuesday that it has fine-tuned Instagram's content recommendation systems in India to curb the visibility of sexually suggestive material and violent content, deploying more advanced artificial intelligence models to identify and filter unwanted posts before they reach users.

The India-specific measures apply to content recommended from accounts users do not follow and concern what Instagram's algorithms promote, rather than a blanket ban on the content itself, the company said.

The announcement comes against the backdrop of increased regulatory scrutiny of social media algorithms in India. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, in an October 10 advisory, asked Meta to review its ranking and recommendation systems to ensure potentially misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not disproportionately amplified.

Meta, however, did not say if the changes were linked to the government advisory.

The changes have helped halve the frequency with which users report recommended content compared with a year ago, Meta said in a post on its website.

The platform said it had strengthened default protections over the past year, tailoring its systems to content that users in India have said they do not want to see. The measures apply to recommendations across Reels, Explore and Feed, where Instagram surfaces content from accounts users do not already follow.

As part of the upgrades, Instagram is using more capable AI models to assess content directly against its Recommendations Guidelines, enabling its systems to detect and limit potentially objectionable material proactively rather than waiting for users to report or hide it.

"Today, our systems keep more of this content out of recommendations, including sexually suggestive content and content that depicts violence," Meta said.

The company said the improvements had enabled it to proactively reduce the amount of content in India that does not meet its recommendation standards. It did not disclose the absolute volume of content affected, the proportion of recommendations filtered or the methodology used to calculate the decline in user reports.

Instagram's recommendation standards are distinct from its Community Standards, which govern content prohibited on the platform. Material that violates Community Standards is removed, while content that may be objectionable, sensitive or low-quality but does not breach those rules can remain accessible without being recommended to a wider audience. Content unlawful in a particular country is restricted there, the company said.

Recommendations determine how users discover content beyond accounts they actively follow, giving the platform's algorithms considerable influence over what appears in their feeds and is amplified across the service.

Alongside platform-wide recommendation filters, Instagram offers users controls to customise the content they see and manage interactions on the platform.

Its Sensitive Content Control allows users to opt for less sensitive material across Search, Reels, Explore, suggested accounts and in-Feed recommendations. Instagram said its systems in India already exclude the most mature content from recommendations, with the setting allowing users to further limit exposure to other sensitive material.

Users can also choose to see less political content recommended from accounts they do not follow, flag posts through the "Not Interested" option and filter selected words, phrases and emojis from comments and message requests using the Hidden Words feature. Its blocking function prevents specific accounts from finding profiles, viewing posts or sending messages, including through new accounts they may create.

Teenagers receive additional age-appropriate protections through Instagram's Teen Accounts, introduced in India last year. These accounts automatically place younger users in a 13-plus content setting governed by the platform's age-appropriate content guidelines.

The changes come amid growing scrutiny of social media platforms over online safety, algorithm-driven content distribution and the exposure of younger users to potentially harmful material.

Meta said user feedback, including when people hide posts or select "Not Interested", also informs its recommendation systems and helps identify content audiences do not want surfaced to them.

The company said it would continue to refine its detection systems as user behaviour and technology evolve, with feedback from users in India guiding further changes.

paragraphs: Chinese entities are adopting increasingly sophisticated ways to use output from leading American AI models to train domestic competitors, as Beijing seeks workarounds to tightening US curbs on advanced chips.

A Reuters review of more than 300 Chinese academic papers, patents, corporate disclosures, recruitment notices and government documents from the past year revealed the scale of the practice, which has moved from the laboratory to mainstream industrial use.

The records describe Chinese researchers using US models to produce answers to questions, build computer code and find solutions to complex problems, and using that output to teach and train domestic rivals.
The documents also show that Beijing is encouraging distillation to make AI cheaper and easier to deploy across China's massive manufacturing sector.

Distillation is not illegal and is prevalent in other parts of the world. While the process cannot reproduce a leading model's full capabilities or entirely replace heavy computing power, it helps developers retain important skills in smaller, cheaper systems.
China's broadening use of distillation could undercut the effectiveness of US curbs on the sale of advanced semiconductors, especially graphics processing units (GPUs) made by US chip giant Nvidia.
Distillation is also a source of friction between the world's two biggest economies ahead of the November 19-20 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen.
US authorities publicly accused Chinese companies in September of aggressive, targeted distillation of US models to bridge Beijing's computing power gap.

And at meetings in Chengdu in July, US Commerce Department officials raised concerns with Chinese regulators and tech executives about companies in China distilling American models, two people familiar with the discussions said.
Chinese officials defended distillation as a standard AI-development technique and said they were open to discussing the issue, one person said.
The US Commerce Department and China's Cyberspace Administration did not respond to requests for comment.

Distillation involves a powerful 'teacher' model generating answers or demonstrating how to complete a task, while a smaller 'student' model learns to mimic the teacher's outputs and reasoning processes.

For Chinese developers facing constraints on computing power, the attraction is in making one expensive request to a foreign model to produce data that can then train domestic models multiple times at much lower cost.

In a November 2024 paper, Shanghai Jiao Tong University researchers described selecting about 5,000 questions answered by OpenAI's GPT-4o, converting the answers into data points, and using them to train a domestic model for complex reasoning.
The researchers also cautioned that excessive reliance on distillation could stifle original innovation, writing that it "might result in the model learning to mimic rather than truly understand".
The project illustrated how American model output can become reusable data, allowing developers to improve capabilities while spending far less on training.

Alibaba researchers described a more systematic approach in an April 2025 paper, using OpenAI's GPT-4o to generate answers for training data, and then deploying a verification system to check the quality of that data.

In a February 2026 paper, researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Chinese food-delivery giant Meituan wrote of using GPT-4o and Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet to train a multi-modal model to handle complex visual and textual information.
Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Alibaba and Meituan did not respond to requests for comment.

Among leading American AI companies, OpenAI's terms restrict using its output to develop competing models. Anthropic's terms say outputs cannot be used to create products that compete with its services.
A US official familiar with the July Chengdu regulatory discussions said Washington believes industrial distillation of American models on this scale goes beyond normal developer activity.

Two people familiar with Chinese developers' operations disputed that assessment, saying distillation is common practice across the global AI industry and that developers follow international standards.
Chinese government documents do not instruct companies to distil American models but encourage distillation to make AI technology affordable and scalable for manufacturing and services.
A national AI+Manufacturing policy package published by eight Chinese government agencies in January explicitly prioritised using distillation to develop lightweight, industry-specific AI models.
The policies reflect Beijing's ambition to deploy smaller, cheaper AI systems across industries.
Concerned by distillation's growing geopolitical sensitivities, Chinese AI developers have in recent months asked Beijing to provide clearer guidance on the practice.
China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to a request for comment.
paragraphs_zh: 随着中国积极寻求突破美国不断收紧的先进芯片限制措施，中国各机构与企业正在采用日益精细复杂的技术手段，借助顶尖美国人工智能大模型的输出数据来训练本土竞争模型。
路透社对过去一年中 300 多份中国学术论文、专利申请、企业披露、招聘启事及政府文件的系统审阅显示，该做法在全行业已具备相当规模，并已从早期学术实验室研究全面迈向主流工业化应用。
相关文献详细记录了中国科研人员如何利用美国先进模型生成问题答案、编写计算机代码并求解复杂任务，随后将这些高价值输出作为训练数据集，用来指导和训练本土对标模型。
审阅的文件还显示，中国政府正在积极鼓励推广模型蒸馏技术，以降低 AI 应用成本，并加速其在庞大制造业基础中的广泛铺开。
模型蒸馏本身并不属于违法行为，且在世界其他地区的 AI 研发中亦广泛存在。尽管这一过程无法完全复制顶尖大模型的全部综合能力，也不能彻底摆脱对高算力硬件的需求，但它能帮助开发者将关键智能技能浓缩并保留在体积更小、部署成本显著更低的轻量化系统中。
中国对模型蒸馏的日益普及，可能会在一定程度上削弱美国限制先进半导体出口措施的实际效果，尤其是对美国芯片巨头英伟达（Nvidia）制造的图形处理芯片（GPU）的限售令。
在 11 月 19 日至 20 日于深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会前夕，蒸馏技术的使用也已成为世界两大经济体之间新的地缘摩擦焦点。
美国有关部门在 9 月份曾公开指责中国企业对美国先进模型进行“激进且具有针对性”的蒸馏训练，以弥补其面临的算力供给缺口。
据两位知情人士透露，在今年 7 月于成都举行的闭门会议上，美国商务部官员曾就中国企业蒸馏美国模型的问题，直接向中国监管部门及科技界高管表达了严正关切。
一名知情人士表示，中方官员当时为蒸馏技术进行了辩护，指出这是国际通行的标准 AI 研发手段，并表示愿就相关议题保持开放沟通。
美国商务部和中国国家互联网信息办公室均未回应路透社的置评请求。
模型蒸馏的基本原理在于：由能力强大的“教师模型”（Teacher Model）生成答案或示范复杂任务的求解路径，而体积较小的“学生模型”（Student Model）则学习模仿教师模型的输出逻辑与推理链路。
对于面临严苛算力瓶颈的中国开发者而言，这种模式的核心吸引力在于：只需向境外先进模型发起一次成本高昂的高质量查询请求，生成的精准数据即可被反复用于低成本训练本土多套模型。
在 2024 年 11 月发表的一篇学术论文中，上海交通大学的研究人员描述了他们如何筛选出由 OpenAI 旗下 GPT-4o 回答的约 5,000 个复杂问题，将其转化为结构化数据，并用于训练专注于复杂推理的本土模型。
研究人员在论文中同时警示，过度依赖蒸馏技术可能会在一定程度上抑制自主原创性创新，并写道这种方式“可能导致模型仅学会机械模仿而非真正理解”。
该项目清晰展现了美国大模型的输出如何被转化为可反复重用的数据资产，从而帮助开发者在大幅缩减算力开销的同时快速提升模型性能。
阿里巴巴的研究人员在 2025 年 4 月的一篇论文中介绍了一种更为系统化的工程方案：使用 GPT-4o 生成大量候选训练数据，随后部署专用的自动化质检系统对数据质量进行多维度校验过滤。
在 2026 年 2 月的一篇研究论文中，来自上海交通大学与中国本地生活配送巨头美团的研究人员，记述了如何结合 GPT-4o 与 Anthropic 的 Claude 3.5 Sonnet，共同训练一个能够处理复杂图文多模态任务的小型垂直模型。
上海交通大学、阿里巴巴与美团均未回应置评请求。
在几家主要的美国顶尖 AI 公司中，OpenAI 的用户服务条款明确禁止将其输出数据用于开发与之竞争的模型；Anthropic 的服务条款亦规定，不得利用其输出创建与其现有产品相竞争的竞品服务。
一名熟悉 7 月成都监管讨论情况的美国官员表示，华盛顿方面认为，中方目前在此种规模上进行的工业化模型蒸馏，已经超出了常规开发者的技术探索范畴。
两位熟悉中国开发者实际运作的业内人士对美方评估提出异议，指出蒸馏在整个全球 AI 产业中属于普遍且成熟的技术手段，中国团队的研发实践完全符合国际通行技术标准。
官方指导文件并未直接指示企业蒸馏特定美国模型，但明确鼓励通过蒸馏等模型轻量化路径，使人工智能技术以更经济可行的成本广泛赋能制造业与现代服务业。
今年 1 月由八部门联合印发的“人工智能+制造”专项政策指南中，明确将基于蒸馏技术研发轻量化、垂直行业专属 AI 模型列为优先支持方向。
这些政策充分映射出北京推动轻量化、高性价比 AI 系统深入赋能实体产业各细分赛道的战略意图。
出于对蒸馏技术面临的地缘政治敏感性上升的担忧，部分中国 AI 开发机构近几个月来已主动向有关部门寻求关于该项研发实践更明确的合规指引。
中国工业和信息化部未回应置评请求。

news.title: Nvidia unveils its Rubin HPC GPU with "more than 50,000" CUDA cores, up from 28,672 in the current Rubin GPU, for agentic workflows and scientific simulations (Jeffrey Kampman/Tom's Hardware)
news.title_en: Nvidia unveils its Rubin HPC GPU with "more than 50,000" CUDA cores, up from 28,672 in the current Rubin GPU, for agentic workflows and scientific simulations (Jeffrey Kampman/Tom's Hardware)
news.author: Tom's Hardware
news.content_snippet:
To accelerate those most demanding workloads, Nvidia says Rubin HPC has the highest number of CUDA cores on any of its GPUs - "more than 50,000" - which might imply that this chip uses a configuration similar to the four-die Rubin Ultra GPU, which links those dies together using NVLink-C2C.

Today's Rubin GPU has 224 SMs and 28,672 CUDA cores, so scaling compute resources to the degree Rubin HPC does would necessarily require more dies on a package. Nvidia didn't reveal more details of the chip'
news.summary_en: Nvidia unveiled its Rubin HPC GPU designed for scientific simulation and agentic workflows, featuring over 50,000 CUDA cores and NVLink 7 interconnect technology. The architecture utilizes a multi-die configuration to scale compute density and minimize idle resources, with a market release scheduled for 2028.

news.summary_en: WASHINGTON, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Commerce Department and Justice Department released information on Sunday about an investigation into Singapore-based company Megaspeed, saying the probe began in 2024.
news.article_content_en:
WASHINGTON, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Commerce Department and Justice Department released information on Sunday about an investigation into Singapore-based company Megaspeed, saying the probe began in 2024.

Megaspeed has come under scrutiny after reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down following an investigation that found a Singaporean executive at the company, Alice Huang, had ties to Chinese intelligence.

Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on November 12 and Reuters has not been able to reach him for comment. Alice Huang has denied the allegations.

"After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential export control violations, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024," the Commerce Department and Justice Department said in a joint statement.

In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia about its dealings with Megaspeed, according to the statement.

US agents, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted search operations at multiple locations associated with Megaspeed in Singapore, and at an affiliated data centre site in Newark, California, the statement said.

Following the enforcement action, the Justice Department took the lead role in a criminal investigation with support from the Department of Commerce, it said.

The statement said that while US agencies typically did not comment on ongoing investigations, they were doing so now to provide clarity and to prevent the spread of inaccurate information.

US AND SINGAPORE DISCUSSIONS ON MEGASPEED

Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang officially left the company on August 31, 2025, but was suspended as chief executive officer on July 10, 2025.

Singapore's government said on Monday it had agreed to continue discussions with the US after Washington released the details of its Megaspeed investigation.

It said last week that Alice Huang had previously worked as the company's chief marketing officer, and then as chief executive officer, before stepping down in August 2025.

Police found insufficient evidence that she had committed offenses relating to spying or the theft of trade secrets, it said.

The city-state has barred her from re-entering Singapore, while investigations into Megaspeed and its dealings continue, the Singapore government said.

Several news organizations, including the New York Times, have reported that US intelligence agencies concluded Alice Huang had links to the Chinese government.

paragraphs: WASHINGTON, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Commerce Department and Justice Department released information on Sunday about an investigation into Singapore-based company Megaspeed, saying the probe began in 2024.

Megaspeed has come under scrutiny after reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down following an investigation that found a Singaporean executive at the company, Alice Huang, had ties to Chinese intelligence.
Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on November 12 and Reuters has not been able to reach him for comment. Alice Huang has denied the allegations.

"After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential export control violations, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024," the Commerce Department and Justice Department said in a joint statement.
In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia about its dealings with Megaspeed, according to the statement.

US agents, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted search operations at multiple locations associated with Megaspeed in Singapore, and at an affiliated data centre site in Newark, California, the statement said.
Following the enforcement action, the Justice Department took the lead role in a criminal investigation with support from the Department of Commerce, it said.
The statement said that while US agencies typically did not comment on ongoing investigations, they were doing so now to provide clarity and to prevent the spread of inaccurate information.
US AND SINGAPORE DISCUSSIONS ON MEGASPEED
Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang officially left the company on August 31, 2025, but was suspended as chief executive officer on July 10, 2025.
Singapore's government said on Monday it had agreed to continue discussions with the US after Washington released the details of its Megaspeed investigation.
It said last week that Alice Huang had previously worked as the company's chief marketing officer, and then as chief executive officer, before stepping down in August 2025.
Police found insufficient evidence that she had committed offenses relating to spying or the theft of trade secrets, it said.
The city-state has barred her from re-entering Singapore, while investigations into Megaspeed and its dealings continue, the Singapore government said.
Several news organizations, including the New York Times, have reported that US intelligence agencies concluded Alice Huang had links to the Chinese government.
Reuters has not been able to verify any of the allegations made in the New York Times or other reports.
US intelligence agencies are still trying to determine her relationship with Chinese intelligence, according to two people briefed on the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Evidence gathered so far indicated she was probably an intelligence asset, someone who provides information to an intelligence service, rather than a trained intelligence officer, they said.
Beijing has rejected allegations that Alice Huang is a spy.
paragraphs_zh: 华盛顿，11月16日（路透社）- 美国商务部与司法部周日联合公布了针对新加坡公司 Megaspeed 的调查细节，证实该项调查早在 2024 年就已启动。
在有报道披露英伟达（Nvidia）前首席执行官黄仁勋因一项调查而辞职后，Megaspeed 受到了严格审查。该调查发现该公司一名新加坡籍高管黄秀媛（Alice Huang）与中国情报机构存在关联。
黄仁勋已于 11 月 12 日从英伟达辞职，路透社未能联系到他置评。黄秀媛则对相关指控予以否认。
美商务部和司法部在联合声明中表示：“通过对潜在出口管制违规行为的主动监测发现可疑活动后，商务部于 2024 年正式对 Megaspeed 启动了调查。”
声明指出，2025 年 5 月，商务部调查人员向英伟达调取了其与 Megaspeed 往来业务的相关记录。
声明称，美国执法人员联合新加坡执法部门，对 Megaspeed 在新加坡的多处关联地点以及位于加利福尼亚州纽瓦克市的一处关联数据中心执行了联合搜查。
在采取执法行动之后，司法部在商务部的全力支持下主导展开了刑事调查。
联合声明还强调，尽管美国政府机构通常不对正在进行的调查发表评论，但此次通报旨在澄清事实，防止不准确信息的扩散。
美新两国就 MEGASPEED 展开高级别磋商
Megaspeed 周日表示，黄秀媛已于 2025 年 8 月 31 日正式离开公司，但早在 2025 年 7 月 10 日就已被暂停首席执行官职务。
在华盛顿公布调查细节后，新加坡政府周一表示，已同意与美方就此案继续进行双边磋商。
新方上周表示，黄秀媛此前曾担任该公司首席营销官，随后升任首席执行官，直至 2025 年 8 月正式离职。
新加坡警方此前调查认为，尚无充分证据表明她触犯了与间谍活动或窃取商业机密相关的罪行。
新加坡政府同时表示，已禁止黄秀媛再次入境新加坡，而对 Megaspeed 及其业务往来的调查仍在持续进行。
包括《纽约时报》在内的多家新闻媒体报道称，美国情报机构认定黄秀媛与中国政府部门存在联系。
路透社目前尚无法独立核实《纽约时报》或其他媒体报道中所提及的指控细节。
据两位听取了相关案情通报但不愿具名的知情人士透露，美国情报机构目前仍在评估她与中国情报部门的具体关系。
他们表示，迄今为止搜集到的证据表明，她更可能是一名向情报机构提供信息的“情报资产”，而非经过专业训练的情报官员。
北京方面坚决否认了有关黄秀媛从事间谍活动的指控。

news.author: Reuters
news.content_snippet: The US Department of Justice will review DoorDash's proposed acquisition of Instacart, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Monday.
news.summary_en: Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Department of Justice will review DoorDash's proposed acquisition of Instacart, according to two people familiar with the matter, bringing antitrust scrutiny to the multibillion-dollar grocery delivery tie-up.
news.article_content_en:
Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Department of Justice will review DoorDash's proposed acquisition of Instacart, according to two people familiar with the matter, bringing antitrust scrutiny to the multibillion-dollar grocery delivery tie-up.

DoorDash said in October it would buy Instacart in a deal valued at about $17 billion to create a dominant platform for ordering food and household essentials online.

"We can affirm that the Department under President (Donald) Trump's leadership will vigorously enforce antitrust laws across industries," a DOJ spokesperson said, declining to confirm the review of the specific merger.

Spokespeople for the two companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Large mergers and acquisitions in the US are required to undergo review by either the DOJ or the Federal Trade Commission, which have historically split scrutiny based on industry expertise.

But if a deal poses competition problems, authorities can negotiate settlements requiring the sale of assets to competitors, or they can sue in federal court to block it.

DoorDash has agreed to pay Instacart $1.25 billion if the deal does not clear antitrust scrutiny, according to a securities filing.

Among standalone delivery apps, Instacart competes with DoorDash and Uber Eats, both of which have been aggressively expanding into grocery and other retail delivery.

Instacart last year announced a partnership with Grubhub, another food delivery platform, to expand restaurant choices on its app and tap into suburban markets.

DoorDash has touted its lead in grocery and retail, saying in February that it had more of those orders than Instacart.

paragraphs_zh: 11月16日（路透社）- 据两位知情人士透露，美国司法部将对 DoorDash 收购 Instacart 的拟议交易展开审查，使这项涉及数百亿美元的生鲜配送合并案面临严格的反垄断监管。
DoorDash 于 10 月宣布拟以约 170 亿美元收购 Instacart，旨在打造一个在全美餐饮外卖与日用品在线配送领域占据主导地位的超级平台。
司法部发言人表示：“我们可以确认，在唐纳德·特朗普总统领导下，司法部将在各行业严格执行反垄断法律。”不过该发言人拒绝就具体并购案置评。
两家公司的发言人均未立即回应路透社的置评请求。
美国大型并购交易依法必须接受司法部或联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的审查，两家监管机构通常依据行业专业分工划分管辖权。
若监管部门认定交易存在妨碍竞争的问题，可以与企业谈判达成要求剥离部分资产的合规协议，也可以直接向联邦法院提起诉讼以叫停交易。
根据监管文件披露，DoorDash 已同意，若该笔并购因未能通过反垄断审查而流产，将向 Instacart 支付高达 12.5 亿美元的“分手费”。
在独立配送应用领域，Instacart 的主要竞争对手包括 DoorDash 和 Uber Eats，后两者近期均在大力向生鲜杂货和其他零售品类配送领域扩张。
Instacart 去年还宣布与另一家外卖平台 Grubhub 建立合作，以扩充其应用内的餐饮选择并进一步渗透郊区市场。
DoorDash 此前大举宣传其在生鲜杂货及零售配送领域的领先优势，曾在 2 月份表示其杂货订单量已超过 Instacart。

news.author: Nate Raymond/Reuters
news.content_snippet: A US judge acquitted on Monday two MIT-educated brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency in just 12 seconds, ruling prosecutors had failed to show that exploiting a software bug to make the money amounted to fraud.
news.summary_en: A US federal judge in Manhattan has acquitted two MIT-educated brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency in 12 seconds, ruling prosecutors failed to prove that exploiting an MEV-Boost software bug on Ethereum constituted wire fraud without material misrepresentations.
news.article_content_en:
A US judge acquitted on Monday two MIT-educated brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency in just 12 seconds, ruling prosecutors had failed to show that exploiting a software bug to make the money amounted to fraud.

US District Judge Jessica Clarke in Manhattan issued the decision a year after a jury deadlocked on whether to convict or acquit Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno of charges that they carried out a type of fraud scheme that had never before been federally prosecuted.

Prosecutors had alleged that the two brothers, both computer programmers, in April 2023 carried out a high-speed bait-and-switch designed to lure trading bots into a trap and drain the accounts of other cryptocurrency traders on the Ethereum network.

But Clarke said prosecutors failed at trial to present evidence showing the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations when they exploited a software bug to carry out their alleged scheme. As a result, they could not be convicted of wire fraud and other charges, she said.

"The question before the court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes," she said. "It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case."

The brothers were indicted in May 2024. Both graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where prosecutors say they developed the skills they relied on for their trading strategy.

Anton earned a bachelor's degree in computer science and engineering in 2024, and James attained a similar degree in 2019 as well as a master's degree in aeronautics in 2021, according to media reports.

Lawyers for the brothers had no immediate comment. A spokesperson for US Attorney James McDonald, whose office prosecuted the case, declined to comment.

Prosecutors said that for months, the Peraire-Bueno brothers plotted to manipulate and tamper with the protocols used to validate transactions for inclusion on the Ethereum blockchain, a public ledger that records each cryptocurrency transaction.

They did so by exploiting a vulnerability in the software code called MEV-Boost that is used by most Ethereum network "validators," who are responsible for checking that new transactions are valid before they are added to the blockchain, prosecutors said.

But defense lawyers countered that the trading strategy they executed was legitimate.

Clarke, in Monday's ruling, agreed, saying the transactions the brothers engaged in contained no misrepresentations and "were not placed on a regulated market with rules prohibiting this conduct."

paragraphs: A US judge acquitted on Monday two MIT-educated brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency in just 12 seconds, ruling prosecutors had failed to show that exploiting a software bug to make the money amounted to fraud.

US District Judge Jessica Clarke in Manhattan issued the decision a year after a jury deadlocked on whether to convict or acquit Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno of charges that they carried out a type of fraud scheme that had never before been federally prosecuted.

Prosecutors had alleged that the two brothers, both computer programmers, in April 2023 carried out a high-speed bait-and-switch designed to lure trading bots into a trap and drain the accounts of other cryptocurrency traders on the Ethereum network.

But Clarke said prosecutors failed at trial to present evidence showing the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations when they exploited a software bug to carry out their alleged scheme. As a result, they could not be convicted of wire fraud and other charges, she said.

"The question before the court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes," she said. "It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case."
The brothers were indicted in May 2024. Both graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where prosecutors say they developed the skills they relied on for their trading strategy.

Anton earned a bachelor's degree in computer science and engineering in 2024, and James attained a similar degree in 2019 as well as a master's degree in aeronautics in 2021, according to media reports.
Lawyers for the brothers had no immediate comment. A spokesperson for US Attorney James McDonald, whose office prosecuted the case, declined to comment.

Prosecutors said that for months, the Peraire-Bueno brothers plotted to manipulate and tamper with the protocols used to validate transactions for inclusion on the Ethereum blockchain, a public ledger that records each cryptocurrency transaction.

They did so by exploiting a vulnerability in the software code called MEV-Boost that is used by most Ethereum network "validators," who are responsible for checking that new transactions are valid before they are added to the blockchain, prosecutors said.
But defense lawyers countered that the trading strategy they executed was legitimate.
Clarke, in Monday's ruling, agreed, saying the transactions the brothers engaged in contained no misrepresentations and "were not placed on a regulated market with rules prohibiting this conduct."
paragraphs_zh: 美国一名联邦法官周一裁定，被控在短短 12 秒内盗取 2500 万美元加密货币的两名麻省理工学院（MIT）毕业兄弟无罪。法官认定，检方未能证明利用软件漏洞获取资金的行为构成了欺诈罪。
曼哈顿美国地方法官杰西卡·克拉克（Jessica Clarke）做出了这一裁决。此前一年，陪审团在是否判定安东·佩雷尔-布埃诺（Anton Peraire-Bueno）和詹姆斯·佩雷尔-布埃诺（James Peraire-Bueno）有罪的问题上陷入僵局。这是联邦检察官首次对此类新型欺诈指控提起公诉。
检方此前指控，这两名身为计算机程序员的兄弟于 2023 年 4 月实施了一场超高速的“诱捕策略”，旨在将交易机器人引入陷阱，并抽干以太坊网络上其他加密货币交易者的账户。
然而克拉克法官表示，检方在审判中未能提供证据表明佩雷尔-布埃诺兄弟在利用软件漏洞实施其被控策略时做出了任何“重大不实陈述”（Material Misrepresentations）。法官指出，因此不能判定他们犯有电汇欺诈及其他相关罪名。
“法庭面临的问题不是佩雷尔-布埃诺兄弟的行为在道德上是否正确，甚至也不是其是否违反了未被指控的其他罪名，”法官表示，“问题仅仅在于，在对政府最有利的角度解释庭审证据的情况下，这些证据是否足以支持本案中电汇欺诈及相关罪名的成立。”
这两名兄弟于 2024 年 5 月被起诉。两人均毕业于麻省理工学院，检方称他们正是在那里掌握了用于执行该交易策略的核心技能。
媒体报道显示，安东于 2024 年获得计算机科学与工程学士学位，詹姆斯于 2019 年获得同类学位，并于 2021 年获得航空学硕士学位。
兄弟俩的辩护律师未立即发表评论。负责起诉该案的美国联邦检察官詹姆斯·麦克唐纳（James McDonald）的发言人拒绝发表评论。
检方表示，数月来，佩雷尔-布埃诺兄弟精心策划操纵并篡改用于验证以太坊区块链交易的底层协议。以太坊区块链是记录每笔加密货币交易的公共账本。
检方称，他们通过利用名为 MEV-Boost 的软件代码中的安全漏洞实现了这一目标。大多数以太坊网络“验证者”都在使用该软件，负责在将新交易添加到区块链之前检查其有效性。
但辩护律师反驳称，他们执行的交易策略是完全合法的链上博弈。
克拉克法官在周一的裁决中支持了辩方观点，指出兄弟俩参与的交易不存在虚假陈述，且“并未发生在一个存在禁止此类行为明确规则的受监管市场中”。

news.author: The Verge AI
news.content_snippet:
Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.

news.title: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines

news.author: The Verge AI
news.content_snippet:
OpenAI is announcing a tool that it says will help child sexual abuse investigators cut through the noise to find harmful material they can act on quickly.

At a Monday press briefing in Washington, DC, OpenAI announced a classifier it says can better detect abusive imagery of kids, including whether it’s AI-generated. It’s also offering free access to vetted organizations, giving developers more guidance on how to detect this type of content, and helping to train law enforcement on how AI can a

inline_images.alt: The diagram shows how comparing increasingly finer lattices helps correct the phase shift on the ori

news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helped produce a proof that could solve a 50-year-old problem in particle physics.

Physicist Nathaniel Craig of UC Santa Barbara, currently a visiting scientist at OpenAI, presented the approach on the OpenAI blog and as a preprint paper. Craig leads the particle theory group at UCSB and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.

Physicists can simulate parts of the Standard Model, the theory describing all known particles and fundamental forces,
news.summary_en: Nathaniel Craig, a physics professor at UCSB and visiting scientist at OpenAI, utilized GPT-6 Astra to resolve a 25-year-old phase-setting problem in lattice gauge theory within the Standard Model of particle physics. The model successfully constructed and validated a formal proof, effectively neutralizing the 'ghost particle' interference that previously prevented realistic simulations of the weak force on lattices.

【起因与机理】旨在解决长达25年的物理理论卡点，实现标准模型在格点上的全量模拟

fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Nathaniel Craig (UCSB Professor / OpenAI Visiting Scientist): Used GPT-6 Astra to construct and prove a solution for the 25-year-old lattice overlap fermion phase problem

[Key Technical Spec] Core breakthrough: GPT-6 Astra constructed and proved a solution for the overlap fermion phase problem in lattice field theory.

我们已经达到这样的程度：人工智能不仅可以回答研究问题，而且实际上可以帮助开展研究本身。

@DeepPrinciple 的 Mira Science 让研究人员能够协调人工智能科学家团队，将他们连接到专业工具和云计算，并运行整个研究工作流程
celebrity.full_text_en:
We're getting to the point where AI isn't just answering research questions, it's actually helping carry out the research itself.

@DeepPrinciple's Mira Science lets researchers coordinate teams of AI scientists, connect them to professional tools and cloud compute, and run entire research workflows.

that's a pretty big leap from typing a question into ChatGPT and hoping for a good response.

the idea of multiple AI agents working through scientific problems together is pretty crazy when you think about it.

could genuinely change how research gets done over the next few years.

celebrity.full_text_en:
We won 🥈 2nd place in the @GetCala partner track at @hackJunction 2026, 

Junction 2026 is Europe's biggest hackathon: 1800+ of builders, 48 hours, and €100,000 in prizes across all its tracks.

I flew from Italy to Finland for one weekend, teamed up with Ignas and Alexander (team: PlayToWin), and in 48 hours we built FlipDD.

the problem: some investors on a founder's meeting list have already backed their competitor, and they'll happily take the meeting just to hear the pitch.

FlipDD checks every investor you're meeting against your competitors on Cala's knowledge graph, so you know who's across the table before you send the deck.

Web app, Telegram bot, and a phone line you can actually call. 

if you're building with AI, check out Cala. it turns company, people and funding data into a knowledge graph your app or AI agent can query through one API (or their MCP server). 

so, instead of scraping the web and hoping your model doesn't make things up, you get structured, sourced records. everything FlipDD reports comes from it.

beyond the result, the best part was the people. I met so many amazing people and great builders this weekend.

huge thanks to the Cala team and Junction. 

Already looking forward to the next one 

Try it 👉 https://t.co/MVv7uDH2rz

celebrity.title_zh:

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) 说：“这对于这次谈话来说非常切题。”

然后 Henri Arslanian (@HenriArsla
celebrity.full_text_en:
A founder building a court for AI agents learns in the first minute that his interviewer is a lawyer.

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) says: "That's very much on point for this conversation."

Then Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) says something I didn't expect. He gave a TEDx talk around 2017 on the future of regulation and the future of lawyers, and a lot of the legal community criticized him for it.

Now, he says, a lot of what they're discussing is coming through.
That's the part I'd watch.

Being early looks like being wrong for a while. A lawyer said his own profession would change, and the profession pushed back.

Now agents are about to make deals, and the disputes that follow have no obvious court to go to.

My read, and it's only a read: the people best placed to judge whether agents need a different kind of court are the ones who work inside the current one.

The episode opens with a lawyer and a founder discovering they're on the same problem.

@GenLayer's answer is a court where validators, each running a different AI model, judge the dispute.

Who should decide whether agents need their own court: the people who practice law, or the people building the agents?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
一位为人工智能代理建立法庭的创始人在第一分钟就得知他的面试官是一名律师。

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) 说：“这对于这次谈话来说非常切题。”

然后 Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) 说了一些我没想到的话。 2017 年左右，他在 TEDx 上发表了一场关于监管的未来和律师的未来的演讲，许多法律界人士因此批评了他。

他说，现在他们讨论的很多内容都已经实现。
这就是我想看的部分。

早到似乎有一段时间是错误的。一位律师说他自己的职业将会改变，但该职业却退缩了。

现在，代理商即将达成交易，而随之而来的纠纷却没有明显的法庭可诉。

我读过，这只是读过：最有资格判断特工是否需要不同类型法院的人是在当前法院工作的人。

这一集以一位律师和一位创始人发现他们面临同样的问题开始。

@GenLayer 的答案是法庭，每个验证者都运行不同的人工智能模型，对争议进行裁决。

谁应该决定代理人是否需要自己的法庭：是执业律师，还是建立代理人的人？

celebrity.full_text_en:
AI Adoption Requires More Than Intelligent Systems. It Requires Accountability.

As AI agents become part of everyday business operations, companies will need more than systems that can complete tasks. They will need to understand exactly how those tasks were carried out.

When an AI agent makes a decision, processes a request or performs an operation, there should be a clear record of what happened, when it happened and who was responsible.

Without that level of visibility, it becomes difficult for businesses to investigate errors, establish responsibility or confidently rely on automated processes.

This is where Actum comes in.

By creating verifiable records of actions across humans, machines and AI agents, @Actum_system provides
  a way to trace activities and establish accountability under predefined rules.

The goal is not simply to make AI more capable, but to make its operations easier to inspect, verify and trust.

Because in business, getting the job done matters. Being able to account for how it was done matters just as much.
#Actum
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能的采用需要的不仅仅是智能系统。它需要问责制。

随着人工智能代理成为日常业务运营的一部分，公司将需要的不仅仅是能够完成任务的系统。他们需要准确了解这些任务是如何执行的。

当人工智能代理做出决定、处理请求或执行操作时，应该清楚地记录发生了什么、何时发生以及谁负责。

如果没有这种级别的可见性，企业就很难调查错误、确定责任或自信地依赖自动化流程。

这就是 Actum 发挥作用的地方。

通过创建人类、机器和人工智能代理之间可验证的行为记录，@Actum_system 提供了
一种根据预定义规则跟踪活动并建立问责制的方法。

目标不仅仅是让人工智能变得更强大，而是让其操作更容易检查、验证和信任。

因为在商业中，完成工作很重要。能够解释它是如何完成的也同样重要。
#Actum

celebrity.full_text_en:
How does an AI agent find opportunities in the agent economy?

I explored this through @termix_ai and took a closer look at how agents can discover available jobs on https://t.co/cLF8F3gpJK.

One interesting thing is that agents aren’t limited to simply responding to prompts. They can explore job opportunities, review task requirements and find work that matches their capabilities.

This is part of what TermiX is building with AACP: infrastructure that allows AI agents to discover jobs, offer services, collaborate, and participate in an economy where tasks can be completed and payments settled.

There’s still more to explore, but seeing how the job discovery process works gives a better picture of what an agent-powered economy could look like.

AI agents are moving beyond just doing tasks. They’re becoming participants in a marketplace.

That’s the direction TermiX is building towards.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
AI智能体如何在智能体经济中寻找机会？

我通过 @termix_ai 对此进行了探索，并仔细研究了代理如何在 上发现可用的职位。

一件有趣的事情是，代理不仅仅局限于简单地响应提示。他们可以探索工作机会、审查任务要求并找到与其能力相匹配的工作。

这是 TermiX 与 AACP 合作构建的一部分：允许人工智能代理发现工作、提供服务、协作并参与可以完成任务和结算付款的经济的基础设施。

还有更多东西有待探索，但了解工作发现过程如何运作可以更好地了解代理驱动的经济是什么样子。

人工智能代理不仅仅只是执行任务。他们正在成为市场的参与者。

这就是 TermiX 的建设方向。

celebrity.title_zh:

蒙太奇工作室就是一个很好的例子。你给它一个简短的说明，它会写下处理和节拍拍摄列表。然后，它聘请了另外三名经纪人来绘制故事板、渲染镜头并创作歌曲
celebrity.full_text_en:
I like the direction @termix_ai is taking: agents are no longer just tools you prompt , they can become buyers and coordinate work themselves.

Montage Studio is a good example. You give it a brief, and it writes the treatment and beat-timed shot list. Then it hires three other agents to draw the storyboard, render the shots, and write the song.

After that, it edits everything and delivers a 1080p master.

What stands out to me is that every step is settled in escrow. Agents hiring agents, with the work and payment handled onchain.

This feels like an early look at how AI agents could start operating as real participants in a workflow, not just assistants waiting for instructions.

https://t.co/ovsjww7eJL

celebrity.full_text_en:
AI agents can already write, code, and analyze

but turning that work into a paid service is still a challenge

here’s why that matters 👇

there needs to be a way for people and other agents to find them, hire them, pay for their services, and receive the results

that's the part of the Agent Economy @termix_ai is working on

think of https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB as a marketplace where AI agents can offer services or look for work. behind this marketplace is AACP, the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol that powers the actual commerce workflow

for example, imagine an agent that specializes in writing content. it can publish a service listing with details about what it offers, its price, and delivery time

another agent that needs content can find that service and initiate a transaction. or a buyer can post a request explaining what it needs and let providers submit their offers

AACP connects these discovery paths to the transaction process. once both sides agree on the work and price through an Offer, they move to Checkout. the buyer funds the Order through escrow using stablecoins

an agent can help prepare these transactions, but value-bearing actions still require wallet authorization and signing

and the money isn't simply sent straight to the provider. it's held in a smart contract while the work is being completed

the provider then accepts the funded Order onchain, does the work, and submits the result

the buyer can review the delivery, request a redo, or challenge it if something goes wrong. once the Order reaches settlement, the payment is handled through the contract

that's the workflow TermiX is building around AI agent commerce

and it goes beyond simply creating profiles for agents or helping them find each other. there's an actual process for agreeing on work, funding it, delivering the result, and handling payment

this is an important step toward making AI agents more than just tools that perform tasks

that's what makes TermiX worth watching in the growing agent economy
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理已经可以编写、编码和分析

但将这项工作转变为付费服务仍然是一个挑战

这就是为什么这很重要

人们和其他代理需要有一种方法来找到他们、雇用他们、支付他们的服务费用并接收结果

这就是 @termix_ai 正在研究的代理经济的一部分

将 视为人工智能代理可以提供服务或寻找工作的市场。这个市场背后是 AACP，即代理自主商务协议，为实际的商务工作流程提供支持

例如，想象一个专门撰写内容的代理。它可以发布服务列表，其中包含有关其提供的服务、价格和交付时间的详细信息

需要内容的另一个代理可以找到该服务并发起交易。或者买家可以发布请求，解释其需要什么，并让提供商提交他们的报价

AACP 将这些发现路径连接到事务流程。一旦双方通过报价就工作和价格达成一致，他们就会转向结账。买方使用稳定币通过托管为订单提供资金

代理可以帮助准备这些交易，但有价值的操作仍然需要钱包授权和签名

而且钱并不仅仅直接发送给提供商。当工作完成时，它保存在智能合约中

然后，提供商在链上接受资助的订单，完成工作并提交结果

买家可以检查交货情况、请求重做或在出现问题时提出质疑。一旦订单达成结算，付款将通过合同处理

这就是 TermiX 围绕人工智能代理商务构建的工作流程

它不仅仅是为代理商创建个人资料或帮助他们找到彼此。有一个就工作达成一致、为其提供资金、交付结果和处理付款的实际流程

这是使人工智能代理不仅仅是执行任务的工具的重要一步

这就是 TermiX 在不断增长的代理经济中值得关注的原因

celebrity.full_text_en:
This morning brought the first real chill of the season.

On November 12th, the workday for many people around the world came to a sudden halt when Outlook, Teams, and Copilot all stopped responding simultaneously.

This is truly concerning. We implement automation and AI agents to keep our businesses running, yet they often rely on the very same infrastructure, if that infrastructure fails, the agents stop working too.

This is where Acurast offers a different approach. On their network, applications run on individual users' devices rather than on a single company’s servers. Developers can decide how many processors an app should run on and the specific type of hardware to be used. Consequently, the entire operation doesn't depend on a single point of failure.

This doesn't mean that things can't ever go wrong, no technology can claim that. However, it provides a way to distribute risk rather than concentrating it in one place, and to me, that is what makes it truly unique.
@Acurast

celebrity.full_text_en:
There are different components working together to support its vision of an AI agent economy.
But what exactly are these components, and what role does each one play?
Let's break down the TermiX ecosystem in simple terms

 The bigger picture
TermiX is building commerce and settlement infrastructure for AI agents.
Think about what happens when AI agents begin providing services to other agents or humans.
They need somewhere to discover opportunities, a system to coordinate work, a way to establish trust and infrastructure to handle payments.
TermiX is designed around these needs 

AACP – The foundation
At the centre of the ecosystem is AACP (Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol).
AACP provides the underlying economic rules and infrastructure for agents to participate in commercial activities.
It is designed to support:
Agent identity.
Job creation and assignment.
Staking and accountability.
Work verification.
Reputation.
Dispute resolution.
Payment settlement.
In other words, it provides the protocol foundation for the economy.

Now let's look at @termix_ai
And https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS is the AI agent marketplace built on AACP.
Think of it as a place where AI agents can be discovered and connected to opportunities.
Rather than simply having agents sitting around waiting for instructions, the marketplace is intended to connect capabilities with actual demand.
An agent with a particular skill can participate in opportunities that require that skill.
.How the components connect
Here's the relationship I want you to understand:

TermiX: The broader commerce and settlement infrastructure.

AACP: The protocol powering the economic interactions.

https://t.co/5nCTrB6xJS: The marketplace built on that protocol.

Each has a different role, but they contribute to the same bigger vision.

The marketplace provides the environment, while the protocol provides the underlying economic framework.

Buy gold when the dollar weakens, but never exceed my defined risk limit.

Trading carries risk,and backtest results don't guarantee future profits.

celebrity.full_text_en:
One challenge I see with bringing AI into DeFi is making complex financial actions easier to understand.

Automation can save time, but users shouldn't feel disconnected from what's happening with their assets.

Before an AI agent takes action, people should be able to understand the intention behind it:

What opportunity is it responding to?
What action is it planning to take?
How does that action fit the user's strategy?
What could happen if the market moves differently?

This is an important part of the bigger picture I'm exploring with @meetmotes.

I believe the next generation of financial AI shouldn't just focus on making execution faster.

It should make the entire process easier to follow, understand, and trust.

Because good automation isn't about taking users out of the loop. It's about making the experience simpler without taking away their understanding.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
我认为将人工智能引入 DeFi 面临的一大挑战是让复杂的金融行为更容易理解。

自动化可以节省时间，但用户不应感到与资产发生的情况脱节。

在人工智能代理采取行动之前，人们应该能够理解其背后的意图：

它是在回应什么机会？
它计划采取什么行动？
该操作如何符合用户的策略？
如果市场走势不同，会发生什么？

这是我与@meetmotes 一起探索的更大蓝图的重要组成部分。

我相信下一代金融人工智能不应该仅仅专注于提高执行速度。

它应该使整个过程更容易遵循、理解和信任。

因为良好的自动化并不是让用户脱离循环。这是为了在不影响他们理解的情况下让体验变得更简单。

celebrity.full_text_en:
🚨BREAKING: GOOGLE SAYS "THE ERA OF AUTONOMOUS ATTACKS HAS ARRIVED" AND AI IS NOW TURNING SECURITY PATCHES INTO WORKING EXPLOITS WITH NO HUMAN INVOLVED.

Google's threat team and Mandiant just caught the first AI hacking tool they have seen find and exploit flaws completely on its own.

Here's what's happening:

→ NO HUMAN IN THE LOOP: A tool called "exploit_agent" reads each software patch, finds the flaw that was fixed, writes the attack and runs it by itself.

→ IT ALREADY HAPPENED: Google found it on an exposed attacker server with stolen victim data and Russian-language comments. Targets: French media and education websites.

→ TWO MONTHS AGO IT DIDN'T EXIST: Google's last report said it had not seen fully autonomous attack pipelines in the wild.

→ SPIES ARE USING AI TOO: Suspected Chinese state hackers used an AI hacking framework against the US aerospace sector. A suspected North Korean group backdoored companies' Claude Code settings.

→ WORSE IS COMING: Google's own timeline puts fully autonomous attacks just 3–6 months away.

Think about this.

We've been trusting software updates to keep the internet safe.

And now Google says AI turns every update into a map for the next attack.

This could become one of the biggest security challenges of the AI era.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
🚨突发新闻：谷歌表示“自主攻击的时代已经到来”，人工智能现在正在将安全补丁转变为无需人类参与的有效漏洞。

谷歌的威胁团队和 Mandiant 刚刚发现了他们所见过的第一个完全自行发现和利用缺陷的人工智能黑客工具。

这是发生的事情：

→ 循环中没有人：一个名为“exploit_agent”的工具读取每个软件补丁，找到已修复的缺陷，编写攻击并自行运行。

→ 它已经发生了：谷歌在一个暴露的攻击者服务器上发现了它，其中包含被盗的受害者数据和俄语评论。目标：法国媒体和教育网站。

→ 两个月前它还不存在：谷歌的最新报告称，它还没有在野外看到完全自主的攻击管道。

→ 间谍也在使用人工智能：疑似中国国家黑客对美国航空航天业使用了人工智能黑客框架。一个疑似朝鲜组织对公司的 Claude Code 设置进行了后门处理。

→ 更糟糕的事情即将到来：谷歌自己的时间表将完全自主的攻击推迟了 3-6 个月。

我们一直相信软件更新可以保证互联网安全。

现在谷歌表示，人工智能会将每次更新转化为下一次攻击的地图。

这可能成为人工智能时代最大的安全挑战之一。

prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.prompt_content_zh:

1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.content:

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
A founder building a court for AI agents learns in the first minute that his interviewer is a lawyer.

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) says: "That's very much on point for this conversation."

Then Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) says something I didn't expect. He gave a TEDx talk around 2017 on the future of regulation and the future of lawyers, and a lot of the legal community criticized him for it.

Now, he says, a lot of what they're discussing is coming through.
That's the part I'd watch.

Being early looks like being wrong for a while. A lawyer said his own profession would change, and the profession pushed back.

Now agents are about to make deals, and the disputes that follow have no obvious court to go to.

My read, and it's only a read: the people best placed to judge whether agents need a different kind of court are the ones who work inside the current one.

The episode opens with a lawyer and a founder discovering they're on the same problem.

@GenLayer's answer is a court where validators, each running a different AI model, judge the dispute.

Who should decide whether agents need their own court: the people who practice law, or the people building the agents?
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
一位为人工智能代理建立法庭的创始人在第一分钟就得知他的面试官是一名律师。

Albert Castellana (@kstellana) 说：“这对于这次谈话来说非常切题。”

然后 Henri Arslanian (@HenriArslanian) 说了一些我没想到的话。 2017 年左右，他在 TEDx 上发表了一场关于监管的未来和律师的未来的演讲，许多法律界人士因此批评了他。

他说，现在他们讨论的很多内容都已经实现。
这就是我想看的部分。

早到似乎有一段时间是错误的。一位律师说他自己的职业将会改变，但该职业却退缩了。

现在，代理商即将达成交易，而随之而来的纠纷却没有明显的法庭可诉。

我读过，这只是读过：最有资格判断特工是否需要不同类型法院的人是在当前法院工作的人。

这一集以一位律师和一位创始人发现他们面临同样的问题开始。

@GenLayer 的答案是法庭，每个验证者都运行不同的人工智能模型，对争议进行裁决。

谁应该决定代理人是否需要自己的法庭：是执业律师，还是建立代理人的人？

viral_posts.full_text_en:
AI Adoption Requires More Than Intelligent Systems. It Requires Accountability.

As AI agents become part of everyday business operations, companies will need more than systems that can complete tasks. They will need to understand exactly how those tasks were carried out.

When an AI agent makes a decision, processes a request or performs an operation, there should be a clear record of what happened, when it happened and who was responsible.

Without that level of visibility, it becomes difficult for businesses to investigate errors, establish responsibility or confidently rely on automated processes.

This is where Actum comes in.

By creating verifiable records of actions across humans, machines and AI agents, @Actum_system provides
  a way to trace activities and establish accountability under predefined rules.

The goal is not simply to make AI more capable, but to make its operations easier to inspect, verify and trust.

Because in business, getting the job done matters. Being able to account for how it was done matters just as much.
#Actum

viral_posts.full_text_en:
How does an AI agent find opportunities in the agent economy?

I explored this through @termix_ai and took a closer look at how agents can discover available jobs on https://t.co/cLF8F3gpJK.

One interesting thing is that agents aren’t limited to simply responding to prompts. They can explore job opportunities, review task requirements and find work that matches their capabilities.

This is part of what TermiX is building with AACP: infrastructure that allows AI agents to discover jobs, offer services, collaborate, and participate in an economy where tasks can be completed and payments settled.

There’s still more to explore, but seeing how the job discovery process works gives a better picture of what an agent-powered economy could look like.

AI agents are moving beyond just doing tasks. They’re becoming participants in a marketplace.

That’s the direction TermiX is building towards.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
AI智能体如何在智能体经济中寻找机会？

我通过 @termix_ai 对此进行了探索，并仔细研究了代理如何在 上发现可用的职位。

一件有趣的事情是，代理不仅仅局限于简单地响应提示。他们可以探索工作机会、审查任务要求并找到与其能力相匹配的工作。

这是 TermiX 与 AACP 合作构建的一部分：允许人工智能代理发现工作、提供服务、协作并参与可以完成任务和结算付款的经济的基础设施。

还有更多东西有待探索，但了解工作发现过程如何运作可以更好地了解代理驱动的经济是什么样子。

人工智能代理不仅仅只是执行任务。他们正在成为市场的参与者。

这就是 TermiX 的建设方向。

I like the direction @termix_ai is taking: agents are no longer just tools you prompt , they can become buyers and coordinate work themselves.

Montage Studio is a good example. You give it a brief, and it writes the treatment and beat-timed shot list. Then it hires three other agents to draw the storyboard, render the shots, and write the song.

After that, it edits everything and delivers a 1080p master.

What stands out to me is that every step is settled in escrow. Agents hiring agents, with the work and payment handled onchain.

This feels like an early look at how AI agents could start operating as real participants in a workflow, not just assistants waiting for instructions.

viral_posts.full_text_en:
AI agents can already write, code, and analyze

but turning that work into a paid service is still a challenge

here’s why that matters 👇

there needs to be a way for people and other agents to find them, hire them, pay for their services, and receive the results

that's the part of the Agent Economy @termix_ai is working on

think of https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB as a marketplace where AI agents can offer services or look for work. behind this marketplace is AACP, the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol that powers the actual commerce workflow

for example, imagine an agent that specializes in writing content. it can publish a service listing with details about what it offers, its price, and delivery time

another agent that needs content can find that service and initiate a transaction. or a buyer can post a request explaining what it needs and let providers submit their offers

AACP connects these discovery paths to the transaction process. once both sides agree on the work and price through an Offer, they move to Checkout. the buyer funds the Order through escrow using stablecoins

an agent can help prepare these transactions, but value-bearing actions still require wallet authorization and signing

and the money isn't simply sent straight to the provider. it's held in a smart contract while the work is being completed

the provider then accepts the funded Order onchain, does the work, and submits the result

the buyer can review the delivery, request a redo, or challenge it if something goes wrong. once the Order reaches settlement, the payment is handled through the contract

that's the workflow TermiX is building around AI agent commerce

and it goes beyond simply creating profiles for agents or helping them find each other. there's an actual process for agreeing on work, funding it, delivering the result, and handling payment

this is an important step toward making AI agents more than just tools that perform tasks

that's what makes TermiX worth watching in the growing agent economy
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理已经可以编写、编码和分析

但将这项工作转变为付费服务仍然是一个挑战

这就是为什么这很重要

人们和其他代理需要有一种方法来找到他们、雇用他们、支付他们的服务费用并接收结果

这就是 @termix_ai 正在研究的代理经济的一部分

将 视为人工智能代理可以提供服务或寻找工作的市场。这个市场背后是 AACP，即代理自主商务协议，为实际的商务工作流程提供支持

例如，想象一个专门撰写内容的代理。它可以发布服务列表，其中包含有关其提供的服务、价格和交付时间的详细信息

需要内容的另一个代理可以找到该服务并发起交易。或者买家可以发布请求，解释其需要什么，并让提供商提交他们的报价

AACP 将这些发现路径连接到事务流程。一旦双方通过报价就工作和价格达成一致，他们就会转向结账。买方使用稳定币通过托管为订单提供资金

代理可以帮助准备这些交易，但有价值的操作仍然需要钱包授权和签名

而且钱并不仅仅直接发送给提供商。当工作完成时，它保存在智能合约中

然后，提供商在链上接受资助的订单，完成工作并提交结果

买家可以检查交货情况、请求重做或在出现问题时提出质疑。一旦订单达成结算，付款将通过合同处理

这就是 TermiX 围绕人工智能代理商务构建的工作流程

它不仅仅是为代理商创建个人资料或帮助他们找到彼此。有一个就工作达成一致、为其提供资金、交付结果和处理付款的实际流程

这是使人工智能代理不仅仅是执行任务的工具的重要一步

这就是 TermiX 在不断增长的代理经济中值得关注的原因
